summary: No zones: the 2022 policy says there is too little evidence of cumulative impact anywhere in the borough.
One off-licence zone in Burnt Oak, adopted in 2020, whose status is unclear because the 2025 policy does not appear to list it.
Two zones covering all premises, in Bexleyheath and Welling town centres, which the council calls saturation areas.
Twelve zones, all for off-licences only, along high streets across the borough; no review of the 2022 assessment has been found.
No zones since April 2025: Bromley and Beckenham town centres were dropped after a 2024 review found too little evidence.
No zones since 2025: Camden Town and Seven Dials were dropped after a 2023 assessment found too little evidence.
No zones: the City decided against them in its 2022 policy, and its draft 2027 policy still has none.
Five zones, all for off-licences only, on main roads and parades across the borough; all kept after a review in March 2026.
Four zones covering alcohol sales, in Acton, Greenford, Hanwell and Ealing, and Southall, redrawn from five in July 2025.
Six zones covering all premises at all hours, including two added at Bowes and Palmers Green in January 2025.
Seven zones covering all premises, unchanged in the January 2026 policy, plus a new match-day policy area around The Valley.
One zone in Shoreditch, re-created in April 2025, plus a softer special consideration area in Dalston, which may account for its Home Office count of two.
No zones since 2021: the Fulham and Shepherd's Bush zones lapsed when their evidence expired and were not renewed in 2022.
No zones; a possible off-licence zone on parts of High Road N17 and West Green Road was flagged for separate work in 2026.
No zones: the 2023 policy has no cumulative impact section, and no earlier zone has been found.
Three zones, in Romford and Hornchurch town centres and an off-licence zone in Harold Hill, under a policy that reached its five-year term in September 2026.
No zones: the 2026 policy says Hillingdon lacks the concentration of licensed premises found in central London.
Three zones in the policy (Hounslow town centre, Heston and Cranford), though Hounslow reports one area to the Home Office.
No zones: the Inn's 2022 policy rules out zoning its precincts.
Six area zones plus a borough-wide off-licence policy, which the Home Office count of six appears to leave out; a review due December 2025 has not been found.
No zones: the council found too little evidence in 2025, though a consultation response asked for zones in Earl's Court and on the King's Road.
No zones since 2021, when the Kingston town centre zone was removed; the 2026 policy again decided against one.
One zone, along Clapham High Street, in force since 2011; no separate cumulative impact assessment for it has been found.
No zones since New Cross and Blackheath were dropped in 2020; a review considering zones is intended for a new policy from April 2027.
Two zones: Wimbledon town centre for all premises, and Mitcham town centre for off-licences only.
No zones recorded in Home Office returns; no published licensing policy has been found.
Five zones since April 2024, replacing a much larger zone that lapsed in March 2023.
Three zones covering all premises (Ilford, South Woodford and Gants Hill), plus nine district policies that set expectations but no presumption of refusal.
Two zones, in Richmond and Twickenham town centres, under review in a draft policy out to consultation until 25 October 2026.
Three zones (Borough and Bankside, Camberwell and Peckham) under review, with a new Elephant and Castle zone proposed in July 2026, plus two monitoring areas.
No zones since July 2023, when Sutton town centre and North Cheam were dropped for lack of evidence.
One zone, Brick Lane, enlarged in November 2024, when the Bethnal Green zone was removed.
No zones since July 2022, when the Walthamstow and Leytonstone zones were removed from the policy.
Three zones since July 2025, Wandsworth's first: off-licences in Tooting and Clapham Junction, and late-night takeaways on Putney High Street.
One zone in the West End, much reduced on 1 October 2026, plus eight softer special consideration zones.
